output.title: Spot proof-of-concept debt before you call it done
output.body:
If you run a 1–10-person business, proof-of-concept debt is the unfinished work you defer during a pilot: missing notes, untested edge cases, a brittle manual step, or a bug you tell yourself can wait until production. The problem is not that some work gets deferred. The problem is letting deferred work disappear into the background.

Use one simple checkpoint at pilot close: is this still just a one-off proof, or is it now something you need to extend into production? If it is a one-off, keep the deferred items in a separate post-pilot list. If it has become a production candidate, pause the rollout and review the deferred list before you expand.

The practical next step is to write three columns before you sign off: what was deferred, why it was deferred, and whether each item is essential before rollout or genuinely post-launch. Review that page with the owner before calling the pilot complete. Treat it as a working record, not a warranty. It keeps the decision in one place and avoids discovering, a week later, that the “finished” pilot still has a small pile of unfinished reality attached to it.
